# Maps in Go

A map is a **key-value** data structure that implements a hash table. Maps are highly efficient for lookup, insertion, and deletion of data by key.

## Map Declaration

```go
// Using make
m := make(map[string]int)
m["alice"] = 30
m["bob"] = 25
fmt.Println(m) // map[alice:30 bob:25]

// Map literal
scores := map[string]int{
    "math":    90,
    "physics": 85,
    "chem":    92,
}
fmt.Println(scores["math"]) // 90
```

## CRUD Operations

```go
city := map[string]string{"JKT": "Jakarta"}
city["BDG"] = "Bandung"     // Create
city["JKT"] = "DKI Jakarta" // Update
fmt.Println(city["BDG"])    // Bandung
delete(city, "JKT")
fmt.Println(len(city)) // 1
```

## Existence Check — Comma-Ok Pattern

Accessing a missing key returns the **zero value** silently. Use the comma-ok pattern for explicit checks:

```go
m := map[string]int{"a": 1, "b": 2}

// Without check — returns 0 if missing
val := m["x"] // 0 — but is 0 real or missing?

// With comma-ok
v, ok := m["a"]
fmt.Println(v, ok) // 1 true

v2, ok2 := m["x"]
fmt.Println(v2, ok2) // 0 false
```

## Iterating with `range`

Map iteration order in Go is **non-deterministic** (random each run):

```go
for city, pop := range population {
    fmt.Printf("%s: %d\n", city, pop)
}
```

## Nil Map Panic

Writing to a nil map causes a **panic**:

```go
var m map[string]int // nil map
fmt.Println(m["k"]) // safe — returns 0
// m["k"] = 1      // PANIC!
m = make(map[string]int)
m["k"] = 1 // OK
```

## Maps Are Reference Types

```go
original := map[string]int{"a": 1}
copy := original // same map!
copy["a"] = 99
fmt.Println(original["a"]) // 99
```

## Common Pattern: Word Counter

```go
words := []string{"go", "java", "go", "python", "go"}
counter := make(map[string]int)
for _, w := range words {
    counter[w]++
}
fmt.Println(counter) // map[go:3 java:1 python:1]
```

quiz.question_en: What is returned when reading a missing key from a `map[string]int`?
options_id: `nil`
Panic
Zero value dari tipe value, yaitu `0`
Compile error
options_en: `nil`
Panic
The zero value of the value type, namely `0`
Compile error

quiz.question_id: Mengapa comma-ok pattern penting saat value map sendiri bisa bernilai zero value yang sah?
quiz.question_en: Why is the comma-ok pattern important when the map value type can legitimately be its zero value?
options_id: Karena tanpa itu Go tidak bisa membaca map sama sekali
Karena tanpa `ok`, kita tidak bisa membedakan key hilang dari key yang memang menyimpan zero value
Karena `ok` mempercepat hash lookup
Karena `ok` diperlukan sebelum `delete`
options_en: Because without it Go cannot read from a map at all
Because without `ok`, we cannot distinguish a missing key from a key that legitimately stores the zero value
Because `ok` speeds up hash lookup
Because `ok` is required before `delete`

quiz.question_id: Manakah pemeriksaan keberadaan key yang idiomatik di Go?
quiz.question_en: Which key-existence check is idiomatic in Go?
options_id: `if m.contains(key) {}`
`if m[key] != nil {}`
`v, ok := m[key]; if ok {}`
`if exists(m, key) {}`
options_en: `if m.contains(key) {}`
`if m[key] != nil {}`
`v, ok := m[key]; if ok {}`
`if exists(m, key) {}`

quiz.question_id: Apa perbedaan penting antara membaca dari nil map dan menulis ke nil map?
quiz.question_en: What is the important difference between reading from a nil map and writing to a nil map?
options_id: Keduanya aman dan menghasilkan zero value
Membaca dari nil map aman, tetapi menulis ke nil map menyebabkan panic
Membaca dari nil map panic, menulis aman
Keduanya compile error
options_en: Both are safe and yield the zero value
Reading from a nil map is safe, but writing to a nil map causes a panic
Reading from a nil map panics, writing is safe
Both are compile errors

quiz.question_id: Mengapa urutan iterasi `range` pada map tidak boleh dipakai sebagai logika program?
quiz.question_en: Why must the iteration order of `range` on a map not be used as program logic?
options_id: Karena urutannya tidak deterministik
Karena `range` pada map selalu berjalan terbalik
Karena map Go selalu terurut berdasarkan hash
Karena `range` pada map hanya valid sekali per program
options_en: Because the order is non-deterministic
Because `range` over a map always runs backward
Because Go maps are always ordered by hash
Because `range` over a map is only valid once per program

quiz.question_en: If `copyMap := original` and then `copyMap["a"] = 99`, what is the implication?
options_id: `original` tidak berubah karena map disalin deep-copy
`original` ikut berubah karena kedua variabel merujuk map yang sama
Program panic karena map tidak bisa di-assign
Hanya `copyMap` yang berubah jika ukuran map kecil
options_en: `original` is unchanged because maps are deep-copied
`original` also changes because both variables refer to the same map
The program panics because maps cannot be assigned
Only `copyMap` changes if the map is small

quiz.question_en: What does `delete(city, "SBY")` do if the key `SBY` does not exist?
options_id: Panic
Compile error
Tidak ada efek yang berarti dan operasi tetap aman
Map menjadi nil
options_en: It panics
It is a compile error
It has no meaningful effect and remains safe
The map becomes nil

quiz.question_id: Mengapa pola word counter `counter[w]++` bekerja baik untuk key yang belum pernah ada?
quiz.question_en: Why does the word-counter pattern `counter[w]++` work well even for keys that have not appeared before?
options_id: Karena Go otomatis memanggil `make` untuk key baru
Karena pembacaan key yang hilang menghasilkan zero value, lalu hasil increment ditulis kembali
Karena operator `++` pada map membuat entry sementara di stack
Karena map string-int selalu diurutkan lebih dulu
options_en: Because Go automatically calls `make` for a new key
Because reading a missing key yields the zero value, then the incremented result is written back
Because `++` on a map creates a temporary stack entry
Because string-int maps are always sorted first

quiz.question_id: Apa tradeoff desain yang disorot oleh example `map[string][]int` pada starter code?
quiz.question_en: What design tradeoff is highlighted by the `map[string][]int` example in the starter code?
options_id: Map memberi lookup per key yang mudah, sementara tiap key masih bisa menyimpan koleksi nilai terpisah
Map memaksa semua slice punya panjang sama
Slice di dalam map tidak bisa di-append
Map of slices selalu lebih hemat memori daripada semua alternatif
options_en: A map gives easy per-key lookup, while each key can still hold its own collection of values
A map forces all slices to have the same length
Slices inside a map cannot be appended to
A map of slices is always more memory-efficient than every alternative
